title: Gene mutant dosage is associated with prognosis and metastatic tropism in 60000 clinical cancer samples.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded Zenodo 20038793 data.zip (34.5 MB), which holds the cBioPortal MSK-MET (msk_met_2021) study: 25,775 samples, 25,775 unique patients, 0 duplicate sample IDs, 42 sample columns including 21 DMETS_DX_* metastatic-site Yes/No columns (liver 8,793 Yes, lung 7,929, bone 7,197, brain 2,921, breast 308); patient file with OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS (10,169 deceased); 230,419 mutations with read counts (0 missing alt counts); CNA matrix over 25,775 samples; three gene panels (IMPACT468 17,602, IMPACT410 6,372, IMPACT341 1,801). From the 3.9 GB results.zip I listed the archive's file index with a ranged download and pulled out only msk_met_INCOMMON.rds (32 MB). Read in R, it holds 224,340 mutations across 21,937 samples, with per-mutation copy number (map_k 1–8), multiplicity (map_m 1–8), purity and posterior-check p-values. Also read the analysis scripts and the Supplementary_Tables.xlsx sheet names (all summary statistics, not per-patient data).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 60,000-sample total and the GENIE-DFCI cohort (Synapse, login needed, not opened); the 46 survival biomarkers / 20 tropism markers; how the DMETS labels were abstracted from clinical records (source study Nguyen et al. Cell 2022, not retrieved). The two large .rds files in results.zip (survival 1.0 GB, adjusted-VAF survival 2.8 GB) were not opened.

a1_downloadable.note: MSK-MET bundle downloaded openly from Zenodo (CC-BY-4.0 record) and the per-mutation INCOMMON calls extracted from results.zip. The second cohort (GENIE-DFCI) needs a Synapse login, so it is out of reach for external validation.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Verified in files: the targets are already columns. There are 21 DMETS_DX_<site> Yes/No columns for metastatic site, plus OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS for overall survival. Nothing has to be constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Mutation table with gene, coordinates (GRCh37), protein change and read counts; CNA gene-by-sample matrix; FGA (fraction of genome altered), TMB (tumour mutational burden), purity; INCOMMON copy number and multiplicity per mutation. All present, no lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Header comment rows describe each column; OS in months, purity in percent (scripts divide by 100), FGA as a fraction, TMB as nonsynonymous mutations per megabase. Labels are binary, so units barely matter.

a5_enough_rows.note: 25,775 patients, one sample each (verified); 21,937 have INCOMMON calls. Rare sites are thin (breast 308, head/neck 390 positives) but common sites have thousands.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.25 GB (78 MB mutations, 28 MB CNA, 32 MB INCOMMON rds, 8 MB clinical)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Tabular data, gradient boosting on CPU. The two 1–2.8 GB survival rds files are not needed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Source study describes ~25,000 patients; files have 25,775. The paper says >20,000 patients were stratified; INCOMMON object covers 21,937 samples with purity filter (25,368 with purity). Consistent once filters are accounted for.

a8_label_provenance.note: Metastatic-site and survival labels come from MSK clinical records, not from a model, and are not computed from the genomic features. Caveat: the GMD features are themselves Bayesian model outputs from the same read counts, so they are inputs, never labels. MET_COUNT, MET_SITE_COUNT and METASTATIC_SITE (biopsy site) are derived from the labels and must be excluded.

B1.why: Five files (sample, patient, mutations, CNA, panel matrix) joined on SAMPLE_ID/PATIENT_ID; joins verified in files.

B2.why: cBioPortal TSVs parsed first try with pandas skiprows=4; INCOMMON rds read cleanly in R.

B3.why: Single institution, but three panel versions (341/410/468 genes) mean genes not on a panel must be masked, not set to zero.

B4.why: Survival is right-censored (15,606 alive); a 'No' for a metastatic site may mean not yet observed.

B5.why: 0 duplicate sample IDs; exactly one sample per patient (25,775 of 25,775), checked in files.

B6.why: Header rows describe columns, but 'Distant Metastasis at Diagnosis' wording vs ever-metastasised is ambiguous.

C1.why: Whether dosage features add held-out predictive value beyond binary mutation status is informative either way.

C2.why: Several tropism/survival ML models on MSK data exist (2021 Nat Commun, BMC, 2026 CNS abstract); none open-weights verified.

C3.why: Likely novel: GMD (gene mutant dosage) features never tested inside a multivariate ML predictor on held-out tumour types.

C4.why: Metastasis is found by imaging follow-up; panel sequencing already exists, so prediction is cheap add-on.

C5.why: Obvious dummies: tumour-type prevalence per site; binary-mutation model; FGA-only model (FGA verified present).

D1.why: ESM-2 could embed mutated proteins, but no backbone fits per-patient panel profiles well.

D2.why: Embedding ~100k+ unique variants with ESM-2 on CPU is slow; backbone likely decorative.

D3.why: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; the INCOMMON package is open source.

E1.why: Hold out whole cancer types (27 CANCER_TYPE values) or panel versions; columns seen in files.

E2.why: 27 cancer types, 90 OncoTree codes, three panel versions; large groups for CRC, lung, breast.

E3.why: Per-cancer-type site prevalence and Kaplan-Meier per type computable directly from columns.

E4.why: One sample per patient, no replicate sequencing; noise ceiling not estimable.

E5.why: Known: FGA (genome instability) tracks metastatic burden in prostate/lung (source study); site prevalence by primary.

E6.why: Label shuffle and dropping GMD feature block are straightforward on the table.

E7.why: GENIE-DFCI needs Synapse login; MSK-CHORD is public but from the same institution and may overlap patients.

E8.why: Paper's tropism/propensity regressions are in results rds and supplementary sheets; scripts included.

G1.why: Hugo gene symbols, GRCh37 coordinates, HGVSp protein changes present in the mutation table.

G2.why: AlphaMissense or OncoKB variant annotations join on coordinates/protein change; MSK-CHORD on cBioPortal.

G3.why: Many mutations per patient need a per-gene aggregation rule before joining.

G4.why: Variant impact × dosage for tropism is a modest extension, not a new question.

H1.why: Patients with and without each metastatic site; 10,169 deceased, 15,606 alive (verified).

H2.why: One institution (MSK), one assay family; 27 cancer types.

H3.why: Claim stated precisely below, restricted to MSK panel-sequenced patients.

H4.why: Single-centre nature is obvious; censoring of 'No' labels is not discussed in files.

I1.why: Caravagna lab (INCOMMON authors) and MSK metastasis genomics groups.

I2.why: Would decide whether dosage is worth reporting in panel pipelines; marginal for clinical decisions.

I3.why: AUROC per site roughly matches a surveillance-imaging decision, but no threshold defined.

I4.why: Tumour type alone probably explains most site prevalence; ML may add little.

J1.why: Tabular modelling, grouped splits, survival models; little transfer learning.

J2.why: Cancer genomics intuition needed for panel masking and tropism plausibility.

J3.why: Clean patient-level feature table plus ablation result is shareable at each stage.

J4.why: Roughly two weeks is plausible but not committed.

J5.why: Kill condition stated below; date not yet written in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: INCOMMON (this paper): Bayesian copy number/multiplicity inference plus per-gene Cox and logistic models
existing_models.score_and_split: Not a predictor; reports 46 survival biomarkers and 20 tropism markers by association testing, with GENIE-DFCI used as a replication cohort.

existing_models.name: Machine learning of genomic features in organotropic metastases (Nature Communications 2021)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; title only from search.

existing_models.name: Metastatic Network model ('Are we there yet?', BMC Medical Genomics 2021)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; search snippet says it combines clinical data and DNA changes to predict organ-specific metastasis risk.

existing_models.name: DSAI-13 CNS (brain) metastasis ML model on MSK-MET (2026 conference abstract)
existing_models.score_and_split: AUC 0.74 on an independent cohort, trained on 25,775 MSK-MET patients (search snippet).

existing_models.name: Deep learning survival model from somatic mutations, lung cancer (PMC10625246)
existing_models.score_and_split: C-index 0.74 vs 0.63 Cox (snippet); used MSK-MET as a cohort.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) for per-variant embeddings, optional; gradient boosting is the real model
backbone.licence: ESM-2 MIT; MSK-MET data licence unclear: the cBioPortal study text says CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, the bundled LICENSE file says ODbL, and the Zenodo record says CC-BY-4.0

integration.join_key: GRCh37 chromosome, position, ref/alt allele (liftover to hg38 needed)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the number of mutant copies matter more for metastatic spread when the mutation is strongly damaging than when it is mild?

controls.positive_control: Recover tumour-type-specific site prevalence (e.g. liver for colorectal, bone for prostate) and the known link between FGA (fraction of genome altered) and metastatic burden in prostate and lung adenocarcinoma.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle DMETS labels within cancer type and confirm AUROC drops to the prevalence baseline; drop the GMD feature block and measure the difference.
controls.external_validation: None openly downloadable: GENIE-DFCI needs a Synapse login. Held-out cancer types and held-out panel versions are the fallback.

honest_claim_h3: Among MSK patients sequenced with MSK-IMPACT panels, adding inferred mutant-copy-number features to binary mutation status does or does not improve held-out prediction of which organs a patient's cancer had spread to, as recorded in MSK clinical records.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a tumour's mutations, copy-number changes and number of mutant gene copies to predict which organs the cancer spreads to.
plain_idea.train_on: Per patient: which of ~468 genes are mutated, the inferred number of mutated copies, copy-number gains/losses, genome instability, tumour type. 25,775 patients (21,937 with copy-number calls).
plain_idea.predict: Yes/No for metastasis to each of 21 organ sites, plus overall survival, taken from MSK clinical records in the cBioPortal MSK-MET study.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tests whether the paper's new 'mutant dosage' feature carries predictive information a standard mutated/not-mutated model misses; a negative result tells clinical-panel pipelines not to bother computing it.

more_or_better_data.why: Same 25,775 MSK-MET patients as the 2026 brain-metastasis model; the new part is per-mutation copy number and multiplicity for 224,340 mutations, which no listed model used.

confidence_score.why: INCOMMON gives posterior checks per mutation, but there are no replicate samples to calibrate patient-level predictions.

models_beatable.why: The 2021 tropism models predate this cohort's release; the 2026 brain model reports AUC 0.74 externally, with unknown split, and no listed model has open weights verified.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The dosage features are computed from the same read counts, purity and copy-number data a strong model already sees, so they are not new measurements; improvement is not guaranteed.

label_elsewhere.sources: MSK-CHORD (cBioPortal, same institution, likely patient overlap; known resource); AACR GENIE BPC and GENIE-DFCI (Synapse login; named in the paper); Hartwig Medical Foundation metastatic biopsies (access request; named in the paper).
label_elsewhere.join_key: Gene symbol and OncoTree cancer-type code (patients do not join across cohorts)
label_elsewhere.why: Another cohort with recorded metastatic sites would test whether a model trained at MSK transfers, but none is openly downloadable and independent.

risks: METASTATIC_SITE (where the biopsy was taken) directly reveals one positive site for the 10,143 metastasis samples.
MET_COUNT, MET_SITE_COUNT and IS_DIST_MET_MAPPED are computed from the site labels themselves.
Panel version (IMPACT341/410/468) correlates with sequencing era and follow-up length, so missing genes can act as a proxy for time.
Gene-level GMD class thresholds (script 3.class_thresholds.R) may have been chosen on this cohort; use raw map_k/map_m instead of the paper's classes.
leakage_plan.split: Main: 5-fold split stratified by CANCER_TYPE, restricted to SAMPLE_TYPE == Primary, excluding label-derived columns. Transfer: hold out whole CANCER_TYPE groups and hold out the IMPACT468 panel. All columns seen in the files.
checks: Shuffle site labels within cancer type: AUROC must fall to the prevalence baseline.
Train on GENE_PANEL plus OS_MONTHS alone to measure how much the follow-up/era proxy predicts.
Compare primary-only against all-sample performance; a big gap signals biopsy-site leakage.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: the leaky columns are obvious and few, but restricting to primaries and masking off-panel genes must be done deliberately.

success_criteria.metric: Mean AUROC over the 8 sites with ≥2,000 positives, within cancer type, on primary samples. This matches the question 'does dosage help rank who will spread to organ X'.
success_criteria.baselines: Per-cancer-type prevalence (AUROC 0.5 within type); gradient boosting on binary mutations + CNA + FGA + TMB without dosage features. No published number on this exact split.
success_criteria.success: Dosage features raise within-type mean AUROC by ≥0.02 over the binary-mutation model on held-out folds, with the gain consistent in ≥3 cancer types.
success_criteria.kill: If the binary-mutation model is under 0.03 AUROC above the per-type prevalence baseline, or dosage adds under 0.005, after one week, stop.

ambitious.why: Publishes clinical-genomics predictors; would need a clear, multi-cancer-type gain from dosage features that also replicates in GENIE.

realistic.why: Publishes ML evaluations of clinical sequencing data; an honest ablation of dosage vs binary features on MSK-MET fits.

fallback.why: Accepts cancer-genomics analyses including negative findings that dosage adds little beyond binary calls.

pitch.headline: 25,775 patients with recorded metastasis to 21 organs, plus open per-mutation copy-number calls for 224,340 mutations, in a 34 MB download.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Per-mutation copy number and multiplicity (values 1–8) from a tumour-only panel are rarely released; here they sit alongside organ-level metastasis labels (liver 8,793, brain 2,921 positives) for the same patients.
pitch.the_win: Dosage features lift within-cancer-type AUROC by ≥0.02 over a binary-mutation model in ≥3 cancer types.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: A clean ablation showing that dosage adds no predictive value beyond binary calls, FGA and tumour type, which tempers the paper's biomarker claims.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Caravagna lab (INCOMMON authors) and MSK metastasis-genomics groups, deciding whether dosage belongs in clinical panel reports.

ml_idea: Build a patient-level table from MSK-MET primary tumours: binary mutation per gene (masked by panel), CNA, FGA, TMB, purity, tumour type, plus INCOMMON map_k/map_m per gene. Train gradient boosting per metastatic site and a survival model. Ablate the dosage block, and test transfer to held-out cancer types and panel versions.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: 25k rows × ~1,500 features × 8 sites × 5 folds with histogram gradient boosting on CPU. The INCOMMON rds loads in seconds in R.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: On primary samples only, fit per-site models with tumour type + FGA versus tumour type + FGA + binary mutations; if genomics adds <0.03 within-type AUROC, dosage cannot matter.

verdict_reason: Labels and features are open, clean and verified (25,775 patients, 21 site columns, per-mutation dosage calls), and the dosage-ablation question is informative either way. But no backbone fits, external validation needs a Synapse login, and tumour type may explain most of the signal. Run the cheap genomics-over-tumour-type check first.
